correctness.summary: The ring-escape identity d_k=r_k M_k, the Type-II backward-window exponent, exact on-axis Gamma invariance, and the divergence-free poloidal-bump non-implication are correct. Two original off-axis assertions were not: off-axis recentering does not preserve the rotation action in general but special fields can still remain axisymmetric, so an iff statement for every particular field is too strong; and the displayed off-axis Gamma-collapse formula tracks only the old swirl component and ignores mixing with poloidal components in the translated cylindrical basis. The repair deletes those claims and leaves the genuine axis-projected escape lemma.

limitations: The compactly supported bump construction is kinematic and does not produce a Navier–Stokes solution.
No actual blowup sequence with d_k tending to infinity is exhibited.
Bounded d_k removes only this geometric peak-escape obstruction; analytic compactness still requires separate estimates.
No universal off-axis Gamma-collapse statement is retained.

originality.summary: The argument is mostly scaling geometry and a kinematic construction built from standard axisymmetric Navier–Stokes variables. A focused literature check did not establish priority for the specific d_k diagnostic, and no priority claim is made.

scientific_value.summary: The repaired result identifies exactly why a chosen peak can be lost under axis-projected amplitude normalization even while backward time becomes ancient. It is useful as a warning for a proposed compactness route, but it is not an NSE blowup construction or regularity theorem.
